requiredConcepts: A moderate earthquake occurred in northern Japan early Monday without reported damage or casualties.
The report distinguishes the headline magnitude from the U.S. Geological Survey measurement rather than forcing one value.
Location and depth are attributed to the U.S. Geological Survey.
No tsunami advisory was issued, and the event was outside the area covered by an existing megaquake advisory.

prohibitedInterpretations: The report is padded into a developed argument with invented theme pillars.
The 6.2 and 6.1 magnitude values are silently merged or one is discarded without attribution.
Absence of reported damage or casualties is rewritten as proof that no effects could later be discovered.
No tsunami advisory is rewritten as a claim that a tsunami was physically impossible.
The prior 7.7 offshore earthquake is treated as the same event as Monday’s inland earthquake.
The contextual megaquake advisory is presented as applying to Monday’s quake.
humanReviewNotes: A proportionate package should contain only a few selected factual claims and no manufactured argumentative structure.
Preserve actor, time, place, distance, depth, magnitude, and agency attribution qualifiers.

source.extractionNote: Five AP story-body paragraphs only; donation prompts, navigation, recommendations, comments, footer, and extension markup excluded.
